answer: An agent economy can make reputation nontransferable by tying each agent’s signing key to a scarce, slowly earned stake: counterparties require a bond before accepting work, then slash it when an arbitrator verifies fraud. Creating a new identity does not erase the attacker’s exposure, because each new key needs another funded bond and time to build history. The delta between the cost of many bonds and the expected gains from deception makes mass Sybil attacks uneconomic; a summit or prism can coordinate review, but neither replaces the stake.
